added.title: Director, Forward Deployed Engineering
added.description:
About Chalk

Chalk is building the data platform that powers the future of machine learning applications. We tear down complexity, latency, and scale barriers that have traditionally constrained ML capabilities. Our platform combines Rust-speed performance with elegant tools that developers love to use. Leading companies depend on Chalk for everything from stopping fraudulent credit card swipes, verifying identities, and maximizing clean energy capture. We've recently raised a $50 million Series A, led by Felicis.

About The Role

Forward Deployed Engineering is where Chalk meets its customers. Our FDEs are exceptional software engineers who integrate Chalk’s platform with the best ML and engineering teams in healthcare, finance, and consumer technology — running technical pilots that win deals, onboarding new customers, and engineering feature pipelines that power use cases like fraud prevention, cancer detection, and product recommendation.

Working directly with our founders, you'll lead this team and define its future. You'll own the strategy for how Chalk engages customers technically — from pre-sales pilots through onboarding, support, and expansion — and build the organization, processes, and playbooks that let the function scale with our growth. FDE is one of the most strategically important and fastest-growing functions at Chalk, and this role will shape what it becomes.

We're in the office 5 days a week. When unavoidable conflicts come up, we’re flexible. This is not a hybrid role.

What You Will Do

Lead, develop, and retain Chalk's team of Forward Deployed Engineers across New York and San Francisco, and own an aggressive hiring plan as the team scales
Define the strategy and operating model for the FDE function: engagement models, account coverage, the pre-sales/post-sales balance, and how FDEs drive expansion within accounts
Own the systems that make the team run — support triage and rotations, escalation paths to Engineering, onboarding playbooks, and the processes for rolling out platform changes to customer environments
Partner closely with Sales and GTM leadership on technical pilots, evaluations, and the technical strategy behind our most important deals
Partner with Engineering leadership to channel customer learnings into the product roadmap and to sharpen the internal tooling FDEs rely on
Stay hands-on: dive into customer architectures, unblock hard technical problems, and set the technical bar for the team
Serve as an executive-level technical counterpart to customer leadership at our largest accounts
Define career paths and growth trajectories for FDEs, and champion the function's identity as we grow — deeply technical engineers embedded with customers, not sales engineering

What We're Looking For

10+ years of engineering experience with 3+ years leading customer-facing engineering teams (forward deployed, solutions architecture, field engineering, or similar)
Strong hands-on technical skills — proficient in Python and SQL, comfortable going deep on customer architectures and data infrastructure
Experience across both pre-sales and post-sales complex enterprise motions: technical pilots and evaluations as well as onboarding, support, and account expansion
Proven ability to hire, develop, and retain exceptional engineers, including senior ICs
Previous experience at an early-stage, high-growth startup
Executive-level communicator who can bridge technical, business, and customer contexts
Experience building the processes and playbooks that let a customer-facing engineering team scale
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent

Bonus points

Previous experience as a forward deployed engineer or FDE leader at a high-growth startup
Experience building production ML systems, ML infrastructure, or data platforms
Experience scaling a customer-facing engineering function from single-digit to multi-team
Experience working with enterprise customers in regulated industries (fintech, healthcare)

Compensation Range: $300K - $350K

Communicates complex technical and delivery topics effectively to technical, business, and executive audiences

To qualify for the role, you must have

7+ years in engineering roles working with private/public cloud IaaS, PaaS, and/or SaaS

Experience with government security frameworks (e.g., NIST controls)

added.description:
URBN is the parent of Urban Outfitters, Anthropologie, Free People, FP Movement, Nuuly, BHLDN and Terrain, operating across retail, wholesale and rental. We are rebuilding our planning technology leadership around a bold thesis: planning is becoming a product
, and the next generation of merchandise and inventory decisions will be made by AI-native, agentic systems
reasoning over our enterprise data — not by manually maintained spreadsheets and rigid legacy tools.

We are seeking an Executive Director to lead this transformation. You will own Planning & Allocation, ERP and PLM technology; carry our enterprise planning platform (o9) to completion; and stand up a product-oriented, agentic planning organization that becomes a durable competitive advantage across all brands and channels. This is a builder's mandate for a leader who thinks like a product executive, is fluent in modern AI, and can partner credibly with brand CEOs, merchants and finance.

Role Responsibilities

Scope of Ownership

Planning & Allocation technology — MFP, Key Item Planning, Assortment Planning, Demand Forecasting, and Allocation & Replenishment capabilities across NA, EU and Nuuly.
Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) — the systems and roadmap underpinning merchandise and inventory operations.
Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) — the technology supporting product creation-to-market flows and its integration with planning.
The o9 planning platform program — drive Assortment Planning to a successful, full rollout across all brands and channels, and own the commercial and delivery relationship with the vendor.
The agentic planning vision — define and build the AI-native forward path for allocation, replenishment and demand decisions, with an internal product team and clear human-in-the-loop governance.
Potential future expansion: Warehouse Management (WM) may be brought into this portfolio over time; the ideal candidate can grow into supply-chain-adjacent scope

Key Responsibilities

Set the multi-year strategy and roadmap for Planning & Allocation, ERP and PLM technology, aligned to brand, merchandising and financial goals.
Deliver the o9 planning platform to full production across all brands and channels, and keep the live footprint stable.
Define and drive URBN's AI-native / agentic planning strategy for allocation, replenishment and demand.
Drive the inventory and financial outcomes of planning — partner with shared teams and brand leads on key metrics and delivery.
Build, lead and develop a high-performing product oriented planning technology team; set the operating model, talent bar and succession plan.
Lead relationships with strategic partners, holding them to commercial terms, measurable value and driving innovation.
Partner with brand merchandising, planning, Finance, Supply Chain and Data Science leaders across the company.
Lead change management so new AI driven capabilities change how planning, inventory and financial decisions actually get made.
Represent planning technology to executive leadership and keep URBN ahead of emerging AI and planning technology.

Role Qualifications

Product-First Approach: Owns the planning vision with a clear roadmap, targeted user outcomes, and measurable business impact—not just a queue of IT tickets.
AI-Native Instincts: Reaches first for agentic, data-driven solutions to fundamentally reinvent how planning decisions are made.
Pragmatic Build-vs-Buy Judgment: Evaluates vendor platforms rigorously, spending capital accountability, and knows when to pivot, halt, or renegotiate.
Deep Brand & Merchant Partnership: Builds trust across brand leaders and seamlessly translates complex business needs into actionable technology.
Bias for Speed & Action: Pushes past endless design cycles to deliver rapid, scalable success across all brands and channels.
Intellectually Honest & Team-Focused: Leads with evidence, recruits top talent, and fiercely protects team focus so critical priorities actually ship.
Outcome-Obsessed: Measures success through core retail metrics (inventory productivity, margin, forecast accuracy, turn, GMROI)—not velocity or story points.
12–15+ years in merchandise/supply-chain planning and/or planning technology leadership, with senior leadership experience in a multi-brand, multi-channel retail environment (retail + e-commerce + wholesale strongly preferred).
Demonstrated ownership of enterprise planning platforms — hands-on experience with a Tier-1 tool such as o9, Blue Yonder/JDA, SAP IBP, Anaplan or Kinaxis, including implementation and adoption.
Deep command of the planning capability set: MFP, OTB, assortment, demand forecasting, allocation and replenishment, and inventory health.
Strong financial acumen — able to connect planning technology to inventory productivity, margin and working-capital outcomes.
Proven people leadership — building, developing and retaining teams, including distributed and vendor resources.
Track record of vendor and commercial management — negotiating scope, controlling cost, and driving delivery accountability.
Strong AI/ML and data fluency; credible conversation partner on modern architecture (URBN's stack favors Python microservices, MongoDB and Node/Vue3), data pipelines, APIs and agentic tooling.
Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain, Finance, Engineering, Computer Science or related field required; MBA preferred.
Executive presence and the ability to influence brand CEOs, merchants and finance leaders.

At Hopscotch Primary Care, we believe great healthcare should be accessible to all people across all communities. Today, almost 20% of Americans live in a rural community, yet only 11% of physicians practice in those same communities. We are on a mission to transform healthcare in rural America. We provide high-quality primary care tailored to meet the needs of our patients through our robust care model and comprehensive care team, delivering care in our clinics, and across settings, and wrapping resources around the patients who need them most.

Our patients and the care teams who serve them sit at the center of everything we do at Hopscotch. Hopscotch Primary Care takes a team approach to serve patient needs and provide the best care possible. Our goal is to provide the care each of us would want for ourselves or for our family members, in the right setting, and at the right time.

Today, we are serving thousands of patients in our value-based care model and the number is growing every day. If you want to bring your experience, skill and passion to make a lasting impact in healthcare, we'd like to meet you.

Hopscotch Primary Care is looking for an experienced and strategic Director of IT. The ideal candidate will develop a deep understanding of the business, our strategy and the technical needs across teams. They will be responsible for overseeing all aspects of our IT department, ensuring the alignment of technology initiatives with our business objectives. Scale clinic and corporate IT operations

Strategic and business-oriented

Data-informed and decisive -
confident making hard prioritization and tradeoff decisions using a mix of qualitative insights, quantitative data, KPIs and expected business impact.

; able to interface with stakeholders, structure work, manage dependencies and maintain momentum amid frequent context switching.

Self-aware and resilient
, able to recognize missteps, learn from execution failures and re-engage with confidence and a bias toward action.

From a cultural perspective, you are:  

Accountable
. You hold a high standard and you expect it from others too.
Someone who treats mistakes as data.
You move fast, name what isn't working, fix it, and carry the lesson forward.
Customer-obsessed.
You build genuine empathy with users, dig into what they actually need, and stay focused on solving real problems.
A problem-solver, not a finger-pointer.
You own challenges alongside your teammates - no blame, no deflection, just shared accountability for finding the way forward.
A contributor who shapes the answer.

Comfortable with uncertainty.
